# Egg, sperm and fertilisation (`reproduction_fertilisation`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/biology.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Life sciences (`biology`)
- Deps: helped by microscope, cell_theory, spontaneous_generation_refuted
- Core idea: In human fertilisation, an egg and a sperm unite. Each supplies one set of nuclear chromosomes; the egg also supplies the cytoplasm and usually the mitochondria. The fertilised egg divides and tissues gradually differentiate, as a series of developing chick embryos illustrates. In humans the fertile window includes the days before ovulation because sperm can survive several days. Ovulation varies between cycles, so counting from the start of bleeding cannot reliably exclude pregnancy. In the usual XX/XY pattern, the sperm contributes either an X or a Y chromosome.
- Pitfalls:
  - Teaching that the fertile days are around menstruation, as 19th-century doctors did by analogy with animals on heat
  - Blaming the mother, her diet or her thoughts for the child's sex or for birthmarks
  - The 'little man in the sperm' or in the egg (preformation), held by most naturalists from 1680 to 1800
  - Presenting the calendar method as reliable; cycles vary
- History: greece: 4th c. BC – Aristotle watches chick development day by day and argues for gradual formation, but has the male supply form and the female only matter; europe: 1651 – Harvey: all animals come from eggs; 1672 de Graaf describes the ovarian follicles; 1677 Leeuwenhoek sees sperm; 1759 Wolff argues for gradual formation; 1780s Spallanzani shows frogs' eggs need contact with semen; 1827 von Baer finds the mammalian egg; 1876 Hertwig sees egg and sperm nuclei fuse in the sea urchin; 1929 Knaus (Austria) studies the timing of ovulation; east_asia: 1924 – Ogino Kyusaku (Japan) times ovulation relative to the next period; americas: 1905 – Nettie Stevens and E. B. Wilson find the sex chromosomes
- Read:
  - Karl Ernst von Baer, De ovi mammalium et hominis genesi (1827)
  - Matthew Cobb, The Egg & Sperm Race (2006)
  - Clara Pinto-Correia, The Ovary of Eve: Egg and Sperm and Preformation (1997)
